role.altitude: She still confers, chooses the massage, proposes the plan, guides the exercises and checks every record. She stops hunting a history row, a technique card and the retype of a clean session note. She does not gain a right to let a list choose the massage, to let a plan stand unchecked, or to file a record she has not read.
reach: Physician: which conditions bar a massage type before a plan is filled.
Physiotherapist: which exercise cards are already cleared for this client.
skills_to_grow: Confer when the history row is blank.
Write the plan by hand when she will not name a massage type.
Guide the exercise when the technique card is blank.
Write the session record by hand when a field will not take the fact.
role.ambitious_version: Return clients arrive with a complete history row and a plan she already checked, so the confer starts from that row. She still decides how massage will help, and no list speaks to the client.

tasks.short: Confer with clients on history, stress and pain to choose the massage.

steps.what: List stored medical histories for these clients.
Confer with clients about problems with stress or pain.
Determine how massage will be most helpful.

tasks.design: {DOCS} lists the stored medical histories for these clients before she confers. She still confers about stress or pain and determines how massage will help. The list does not record the confer, does not raise an alert, and does not send a note.
tasks.previous_blocker: The history sat in a free-text note, so a list had no stable fields to show.
tasks.enabler_now: The clinic can keep conditions, pain areas, allergies and last massage type as fields in {DOCS}, and a configured list shows only those.
tasks.still_hard: A first visit has no row, and she still has to hear how the client is today. The list cannot decide the massage.
tasks.human_edge: She hears how the client describes the pain and decides what massage can and cannot do.
tasks.altitude: She stops hunting the old note. She still confers and still determines how massage will help. She gains no right to skip the conversation.

reach.learn: Which conditions she must ask about when the history row is blank.

evidence.claim: Health data is a special category of personal data.
A usage log that measures clinicians needs works-council consent.
On return visits the only time that can disappear is the history lookup. The confer does not get shorter. This range is model knowledge, not a measured study.

assumptions: Reception keeps, outside this task and not counted as time saved here, the fields client name, conditions, pain areas, allergies and last massage type.
If any of those fields is blank, the list returns no row and she asks during the confer, which stays at full time.
The list does not extract a history from free text, does not record the confer, and does not score her work.
Upkeep of 0.2 hours per 100 baseline hours is telling reception when a field will not list.
unknowns: Whether reception or the therapist maintains those history fields today.
Whether this company's massage note is treated as a medical dossier.
research_questions: How often is the history row complete before a return visit?

incremental.description: Tell reception when a history field will not list.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is a week of first visits with no stored history, so the list is empty and the confer stays the whole task. High is a week of return clients whose history row is complete, and only the short lookup disappears. She still confers and determines the aim at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop and propose treatment plans that name the massage types.

steps.what: Develop which massage types the treatment plans should specify.
Fill treatment plan v1 with those massage types.
Check the plan still specifies the massage types she chose.
Propose that treatment plan to the client.

tasks.design: She develops the massage types, and a separate step fills treatment plan v1 in {DOCS} with those types only. She checks that the plan still specifies them, then proposes it to the client. The fill does not choose the types, does not raise an alert, and does not send the plan.
tasks.previous_blocker: The plan was a paragraph she composed, so there was nothing a template could copy without choosing the massage for her.
tasks.enabler_now: A template with type, body area, minutes and what to avoid can be filled by a deterministic copy of the types she has already named.
tasks.still_hard: The wrong type can harm. She still chooses, still checks the wording, and still proposes the plan herself. No model picks the massage.
tasks.human_edge: She chooses the massage types and stands behind the plan she proposes to the client.
tasks.altitude: She stops retyping a plan whose types she has already named. She still develops the types, still checks the plan, and still proposes it. A filled plan does not stand until she accepts it.

reach.task: Set which massage types are allowed for this client
reach.learn: Which massage types the physiotherapist has already ruled out.

evidence.claim: Health data is a special category of personal data.
A medical dossier is kept 20 years from the last change, shared only with consent, and an access log is available on request.
The copy into the plan is the only slice that can disappear, and only after she has named the types. This range is model knowledge, not a measured study.

assumptions: She names massage type, body area, minutes and what to avoid in the develop step. That time stays in the task.
The clinic keeps those field names on the template outside this task. The fill copies only the types she named and does not choose them.
If she will not name a type, or a field is missing, the fill does not run and she writes the plan by hand. There is no always-on second write step.
A later change voids ap-plan. She corrects the plan by hand.
If the plan is a medical dossier, retention follows the rule the clinic already uses. This fill does not record who viewed it.
The meaning check is time she already spends reading what was written. It is not extra upkeep. Upkeep of 0.3 hours is telling the clinic when a field will not take a type.
unknowns: Whether the client must consent again before this plan is stored.
Whether a workplace massage plan is a medical dossier kept for 20 years.
research_questions: Which massage types does this clinic allow on a plan?

incremental.description: Tell the clinic when a plan field will not take a massage type.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is sessions where she will not name the massage types in the template, so the fill does not run and she writes the plan by hand. High is sessions where she names type, area and minutes and only the copy into treatment plan v1 disappears. She still develops, checks and proposes at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Guide clients on posture, stretching, strengthening and relaxation exercises.

steps.what: List stored information on postural techniques and exercises.
Decide between stretching, strengthening and postural improvement.
Provide clients guidance on relaxation and rehabilitative exercises.

tasks.design: {DOCS} lists the clinic's stored technique cards. She decides which one fits and still provides the guidance in person. The list does not fill a handout, does not raise an alert, and does not send the exercises.
tasks.previous_blocker: Technique notes were not filed as named cards, so she hunted a folder before she could show the movement.
tasks.enabler_now: A physiotherapist can keep cards in {DOCS} with a technique name, an aim and what to avoid, and a configured list shows those cards.
tasks.still_hard: Showing the movement and seeing whether this client can do it stays with her. A card does not guide the client.
tasks.human_edge: She shows the movement and adapts it to the body in front of her.
tasks.altitude: She stops hunting the technique folder. She still decides which exercise fits and still guides the client. She gains no right to hand the exercise to a list.

reach.task: Keep the rehabilitative exercise cards current
reach.learn: Which technique cards the physiotherapist maintains, and which aims they cover.

evidence.claim: Health data is a special category of personal data.
A usage log that measures clinicians needs works-council consent.
Looking up a card is the only slice that can disappear. Guiding the client does not get shorter. This range is model knowledge, not a measured study.

assumptions: A physiotherapist keeps, outside this task and not counted as time saved here, the fields technique name, aim and what to avoid.
Tying a named technique to this client's pain is health data. The card library itself is the clinic's technique names.
If the card is blank, the list returns nothing and she still provides the guidance at full time from what she knows.
The list does not demonstrate the exercise, does not fill a handout, and does not record the session or score her teaching.
Upkeep of 0.2 hours per 100 baseline hours is telling the physiotherapist when a card is blank or wrong.
unknowns: Whether technique cards are maintained by a physiotherapist or by the massage therapist.
research_questions: Who is allowed to add or retire a technique card?

incremental.description: Tell the physiotherapist when a technique card is blank or wrong.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is days with no technique card, so she guides from what she knows and the lookup saves nothing. High is days she looks up one stored card and still demonstrates the exercise herself at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain the treatment record after each session.

steps.what: Decide which session facts the treatment records must maintain.
Fill treatment record v1 with the facts she named.
Check the treatment record still means this session.

tasks.design: She names the session facts, and a separate step fills treatment record v1 in {DOCS} with those facts only. She checks the meaning before the record stands. The fill does not raise an alert, does not send the record, and does not draft it from a recording.
tasks.previous_blocker: The record was a narrative she typed, and a generated note from speech is the wrong tool: checked studies of scribes still find errors in the note.
tasks.enabler_now: Body area, massage type and a short response can be copied into {DOCS} by deterministic fields once she has named them. No model writes the note.
tasks.still_hard: A one-line response does not fit every session. She still decides what the record must say, and she still reads it before it stands.
tasks.human_edge: She was in the session. She will not let a record stand that says something else happened.
tasks.altitude: She stops retyping a note whose facts she has already named. She still decides those facts and still checks the record. An unchecked record does not stand, and she does not gain a right to skip the reading.

reach.task: Read the treatment record before the next clinical decision
reach.learn: Which of area, massage type and response the physician expects in the short record.

evidence.claim: Health data is a special category of personal data.
A medical dossier is kept 20 years from the last change, shared only with consent, and an access log is available on request.
A preprint found verified errors in 31.3% of 565 notes from three scribes on recorded or simulated consults.
Only the copy of already named facts into the record can disappear, and only on sessions that fit the short fields. This range is model knowledge, not a measured study of massage records.

assumptions: She names body area, massage type used and a short client response in the decide step. That time stays in the task. No recording is made.
The clinic keeps those field names outside this task. The fill copies only those fields and does not interpret the response.
If the response will not fit one short line, or a field is missing, the fill does not run and she writes the record by hand. There is no always-on second write step.
A later change voids ap-record. She corrects the record by hand.
The meaning check is time she already spends reading what was written. It is not extra upkeep.
If this note is a medical dossier, retention follows the rule the clinic already uses. This fill does not record who viewed it and is not a usage log of her work.
Upkeep of 0.4 hours per 100 baseline hours is telling the clinic when a field will not take a fact.
unknowns: Whether a workplace massage note is a medical dossier kept for 20 years.
Who besides the therapist is allowed to read the treatment record.
research_questions: Is this company's massage note a medical dossier under national rules?

incremental.description: Tell the clinic when a record field will not take the session fact.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is sessions whose response will not fit the short fields, so the fill does not run and she writes the whole record by hand. High is sessions where area, type and a one-line response all fit, and only the copy into treatment record v1 disappears. She still names the facts and checks the meaning at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
